seo_title: Delhi HC Returns 17 IP Suits Over Jurisdiction
title: Delhi High Court Returns 17 IP Suits, Including Beiersdorf and SAIC-Linked Matters, for Want of Territorial Jurisdiction
case_name: ABD Maestro Pvt. Ltd. v. Great Galleon Ventures Ltd. and connected matters
citation: CS(COMM) 987/2026 with I.A. 24805-24807/2026, and connected suits; judgment dated 3 November 2026 (reserved 24 September 2026)
card_summary: Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav of the Delhi High Court returned 17 commercial IP suits for want of territorial jurisdiction, among them matters naming Beiersdorf, an SAIC Motor-linked dealer and an Amazon Seller entity. The court held that website accessibility in Delhi, or an order delivered there, does not by itself found jurisdiction, and applied forum non conveniens where neither side had a Delhi connection.
card_tip: A plaintiff suing a company absent from Delhi should not rely on a website being viewable there or a trap purchase delivered there; file where the defendant or cause of action sits, or risk the suit being returned.
verification_notes: The case number CS(COMM) 987/2026, the bench (Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav, sole judge), the reserved date of 24 September 2026 and pronouncement on 3 November 2026 were read directly from the judgment on Indian Kanoon. The 17-suit figure and the named defendants (Beiersdorf, an SAIC Motor-linked dealer, Amazon Seller Services) are reported by MLex and corroborated by Bar and Bench and SpicyIP. The judgment text opened ran only to its discussion of governing precedent (paragraph 43 of a longer order); the application of the test to each of the 17 suits and the exact relief granted to each named defendant was not independently confirmed, so the card states the general holding rather than suit-by-suit outcomes. This ruling is a separate, later development from the territorial-jurisdiction reference in HUL v. Kwick Living (25 August 2026, already reported elsewhere), which a Full Bench reserved on 6 November 2026; the two are not the same ruling.
